title: Long and short notes
summary: Whole, half and quarter notes: how many beats each note lasts.

steps.title: Quarter note
steps.body:
A **quarter note** lasts one beat. Four of them fill a bar of four beats. It is drawn as a filled-in dot with a stem.

**Why it matters:** It is the basic unit you count in. When you tap a steady beat you are tapping quarter notes.

steps.title: Half note
steps.body:
A **half note** lasts two beats: tap on one and hold through two. It is drawn as a hollow dot with a stem.

**Why it matters:** Long notes give music room to breathe. Ballad chords often last a half note or longer.

steps.title: Whole note
steps.body:
A **whole note** lasts four beats, a whole bar of four. It is drawn as a hollow dot with no stem.

**Why it matters:** On a chart, a chord held for a whole note means "play it once and let it ring for the bar".

steps.title: One bar, three ways
steps.body: A whole note, two half notes, or four quarter notes: each fills a bar of four beats.

items.prompt: Tap two half notes: 2 taps, each held for two beats.
Tap a whole note: 1 tap, held for the whole bar.

steps.title: Mix them
steps.body: Play a C chord as a whole note, then two half notes, then four quarter notes. Count out loud the whole time.

items.prompt: How many quarter notes last as long as one half note?
How many half notes last as long as one whole note?
Tap a half note, then two quarter notes: 3 taps.
